# Zumly — Complete LLM Reference

> JavaScript library for hierarchical zoom navigation (ZUI). Navigate in Z (depth) through discrete views in the XY plane with spatial transitions.

Version: 1.0.0
License: MIT
Author: Juan Martin Muda — Zumerlab
Repository: https://github.com/zumerlab/zumly
Site: https://zumerlab.com/zumly/ · Showcases: https://zumerlab.com/zumly/#/home/showcases · Learn in six steps: https://zumerlab.com/zumly/learn/ · API reference: https://zumerlab.com/zumly/api.html
npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/zumly

## 1. What Zumly Is (and Is Not)

Zumly is a structured, trigger-driven zoom user interface engine. Users zoom into focused elements to open the next view — attention (focus) and depth (Z) stay aligned with layout (XY).

It is NOT:
- A freeform pan/zoom canvas (like Miro or Figma)
- A map library (like Leaflet or Mapbox)
- A slide/carousel library

It IS:
- Framework-agnostic: works with React, Vue, Svelte, Angular, or plain HTML
- Pluggable transition drivers: CSS, WAAPI, Anime.js, GSAP, Motion, none, or custom
- Plugin system with hash router included
- Touch, keyboard, mouse, and wheel input support

### Key Concepts

- **Canvas**: Container element with class `zumly-canvas` where views render
- **View**: A DOM subtree with root class `z-view`. Sources: HTML strings, URLs, async functions, objects with `render()`, web components
- **Trigger**: Element with class `zoom-me` and `data-to="viewName"` that initiates zoom-in
- **Depth navigation**: Zoom in/out through view hierarchy (Z axis)
- **Lateral navigation**: Navigate between sibling views at the same depth level
- **Driver**: Pluggable animation engine for transitions
- **Plugin**: Object with `install(instance, options)` or plain function

---

## 2. Installation

### npm / yarn / pnpm

```bash
npm install zumly
```

### ESM import

```js
import Zumly from 'zumly'
import 'zumly/style.css'
```

### CDN (unpkg)

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/zumly/dist/zumly.css">
<script src="https://unpkg.com/zumly/dist/zumly.js"></script>
```

When using the CDN, `Zumly` is available as a global (`window.Zumly`).

### Package exports

```
"zumly"            → main entry (ESM: dist/zumly.mjs, CJS: dist/zumly.js)
"zumly/style.css"  → dist/zumly.css
"zumly/css"        → dist/zumly.css
"zumly/drivers"    → src/drivers/index.js (all built-in drivers)
"zumly/driver-helpers" → src/drivers/driver-helpers.js (helpers for custom drivers)
```

---

## 3. Quick Start

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/zumly/dist/zumly.css">
<script src="https://unpkg.com/zumly/dist/zumly.js"></script>

<div class="zumly-canvas" id="app"></div>

<script>
  const app = new Zumly({
    mount: '#app',
    initialView: 'home',
    views: {
      home: '<div class="z-view"><div class="zoom-me" data-to="detail">Open</div></div>',
      detail: '<div class="z-view"><p>Detail view</p></div>'
    }
  });
  app.init();
</script>
```

---

## 4. Constructor Options (Full Reference)

```js
new Zumly({
  // ─── Required ────────────────────────────
  mount: '#app',              // CSS selector or HTMLElement; gets class zumly-canvas and fills its nearest positioned ancestor (give it a size)
  initialView: 'home',       // Name of the first view to show
  views: {                    // Map of view names → view sources
    home: '<div class="z-view">...</div>',
    detail: detailViewFunction,
  },

  // ─── Optional ────────────────────────────
  preload: ['detail'],        // View names to resolve and cache on init()
  debug: false,               // Enable debug messages in console
  deferred: false,            // Render view content after zoom animation completes
  componentContext: new Map(), // Context object passed to function/object view sources

  // ─── Transitions ─────────────────────────
  transitions: {
    driver: 'css',            // 'css' | 'waapi' | 'none' | 'anime' | 'gsap' | 'motion' | Function
    cover: 'width',           // 'width' | 'height' — which dimension to use for cover scale
    duration: '1s',           // CSS time ('600ms') or number of ms (600)
    ease: 'ease-in-out',      // CSS easing; all drivers follow the same curve. anime/gsap/motion also accept their own ease names
    effects: ['blur(3px)', 'blur(8px) saturate(0)'],  // CSS filter for [previousView, lastView]
    animateEffects: true,     // false applies the effects at once instead of animating them (smoother with heavy views)
    stagger: 0,               // Progressive delay (ms) between view layers
    parallax: 0,              // Parallax intensity (0-1) — reserved for future use
    hideTrigger: false,        // 'fade' | true | false — hide trigger element during zoom
  },

  // ─── Depth navigation UI ─────────────────
  depthNav: {                 // true = default, false = disabled, or object:
    position: 'bottom-left',  // 'bottom-left' | 'top-left'
    style: 'button',          // 'button' | 'title' | 'rings'
  },

  // ─── Lateral navigation UI ───────────────
  lateralNav: {               // true = default, false = disabled, or object:
    mode: 'always',           // 'always' = whenever siblings exist, 'auto' = only when view doesn't cover full canvas
    arrows: true,             // Show prev/next arrow buttons
    dots: true,               // Show dot indicators
    keepAlive: false,         // true = keep lateral views in DOM (hidden), 'visible' = keep visible
    position: 'bottom-center', // 'bottom-center' | 'top-center'
    siblings: null,           // Declared sibling order: ['a','b','c'] or { parentView: ['a','b','c'] }
    swipe: false,             // Horizontal swipe moves between siblings instead of zooming out
  },

  // ─── Input controls ──────────────────────
  inputs: {
    wheel: true,              // Wheel zoom-out
    keyboard: true,           // Arrow keys
    click: true,              // Click/mouseup
    touch: true,              // Touch/swipe
    pinch: false,             // Closing two fingers zooms out (opt-in)
  },

  // ─── Gestures ────────────────────────────
  gestures: {                 // true = { follow: true }; default false
    follow: false,            // Trackpad, swipe and pinch drive the zoom-out with their progress
    threshold: 0.5,           // Releasing past this progress (0-1) finishes it
  },

  // ─── Heavy views ─────────────────────────
  rasterize: {                // true = global snapdom (no stream); default false
    snapdom,                  // import { snapdom } from '@zumer/snapdom'
    stream,                   // import { stream } from '@zumer/snapdom-plugins/stream': keeps the photo current
    minNodes: 800,            // Lighter views are photographed only if they use backdrop-filter
    scale: 1,                 // Resolution of the photo (1-4)
  },
  webgl: {                    // true = global snapdom; brings rasterize (same settings); default false
    effects: {},              // More effects for transitions.effects, by name, in GLSL
    glass: false,             // The photo of a view coming in keeps its backdrop-filter (slower)
    hover: false,             // Build and photograph a view while the pointer rests on its trigger
    ancestors: true,          // Past the third level, keep everything behind as one picture
  },

  // ─── Navigation labels (aria-label) ──────
  labels: {                   // false = none; each: template, function, or false
    back: 'Back to {title}',
    prev: 'Previous sibling view',
    next: 'Next sibling view',
    goTo: 'Go to {title}',
  },
})
```

### Option Details

#### `transitions.driver`

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `'css'` | CSS transitions (default). Zero JS animation overhead. |
| `'waapi'` | Web Animations API. JS-controlled with CSS performance. |
| `'none'` | Instant transitions. Great for testing. |
| `'anime'` | Anime.js v4 or v3 from the global `anime`. With a bundler: `animeDriver(anime)` from `'zumly'`. |
| `'gsap'` | GSAP from the global `gsap`. With a bundler: `gsapDriver(gsap)`. |
| `'motion'` | Motion from the global `Motion`. With a bundler: `motionDriver({ animate })`. |
| `function` | Custom driver function `(spec, onComplete) => void` |

For a CSS `ease`, every driver follows the same curve (library drivers apply it per layer, so `stagger` does not distort it). Library drivers finish at their deadline when the tab is hidden and ignore late library callbacks.

#### `transitions.cover`

Controls how the zoom scale is calculated. `'width'` scales the child view so its width matches the trigger width. `'height'` uses height instead. Can be overridden per trigger with `data-with-cover="height"`.

#### `transitions.effects`

Array of 1-2 CSS filter strings applied to background views during zoom. First applies to previousView, second to lastView. If only one is provided, it is used for both. The lastView is scaled by the level before it too, so its `blur()` radius is divided by that scale: the blur stays what you wrote instead of growing with depth. Can be overridden per trigger with `data-with-effects="blur(3px) | blur(8px) saturate(0)"`.

#### `transitions.animateEffects`

Boolean, default `true`: the effects' filter transitions together with the zoom. `false` applies the filter at once when the zoom starts (and removes it at once on zoom-out). Animating a filter on large background layers is the costliest part of a transition with heavy views; turning it off took a ~3000-node view from about 27 to 19.5 ms per frame. The transition length can also be set in CSS with `--z-effect-duration` on `.z-view`.

#### `transitions.hideTrigger`

- `false` (default): trigger stays visible during zoom
- `true`: trigger gets `visibility: hidden` during zoom
- `'fade'`: trigger crossfades with the incoming view (opacity transition)

With `false` or `true`, a zoom-out fades the view into its trigger over the last third of the motion (opacity only, with any driver), so the trigger takes its place instead of the view vanishing at the end.

Can be overridden per trigger with `data-hide-trigger` or `data-hide-trigger="fade"`.

#### `transitions.stagger`

Progressive delay in milliseconds between view layers. Current view starts immediately, previous view after `1 * stagger` ms, last view after `2 * stagger` ms. Default: 0 (all layers animate together).

#### `lateralNav.mode`

- `'always'` (default): lateral nav appears whenever sibling views exist at current depth
- `'auto'`: lateral nav only appears when the current view doesn't cover the full canvas

Siblings are the views of the other `.zoom-me[data-to]` triggers in the parent view, so each depth level has its own group. A trigger with `data-sibling="false"` is left out of the group. Several triggers opening the same view with different `data-*` (`data-id`, …) are separate siblings, one per trigger (see Lateral Navigation).

#### `lateralNav.keepAlive`

- `false` (default): lateral views are removed from DOM when navigating away
- `true`: views are kept in DOM with `display: none` (class `is-lateral-hidden`)
- `'visible'`: views are kept in DOM and remain visible (for CSS-based transitions between siblings)

#### `lateralNav.siblings`

Declared sibling order for lateral navigation. Takes precedence over inferring order and slide direction from trigger positions in the parent view; non-adjacent jumps slide proportionally further.

- Array form (one lateral group): `siblings: ['today', 'tomorrow', 'week']`
- Map form (keyed by parent view name): `siblings: { home: ['today', 'tomorrow', 'week'] }`
- An array applies to whichever parent has the current view among its names; with several levels, prefer the map.
- A sibling that shares its view with others is named with its data: `siblings: ['room?id=kitchen', 'room?id=bedroom']`.

#### `depthNav`

Depth navigation is the back button. It only appears when depth > 0 (i.e., you've zoomed in at least once). If the current view already contains a `.z-depth-nav` (e.g., from a nested Zumly instance, or a back button of your own), the built-in one is suppressed.

Styles:
- `'button'` (default): a dot in its ring (the sibling bar keeps the chevrons).
- `'title'`: a dot in its ring plus the title of the view above.
- `'rings'`: a dot inside one ring per level above (up to 6; innermost = right above). A tap zooms out one level; hover, a long press or ArrowUp opens a band per level (`.z-depth-fan` > `.z-depth-band`) to jump several levels in one transition. Rings and bands carry `z-depth-ring--up-N` / `z-depth-band--up-N` (1 = right above), `--depth-N` (0 = root) and `data-view`, so CSS can mark a level: `.z-depth-ring[data-view="security"] { stroke: tomato }`. With `gestures.follow`, `--z-grow` (0-1) and `.is-past-threshold` on `.z-depth-nav` let the dot grow into its ring.

When the back button and the sibling bar share an edge, the bar is shifted aside (`--z-nav-shift-x`) or stacked above the button (`--z-nav-shift-y`) so they never overlap.

#### `gestures`

With `follow: true`, the trackpad (two-finger scroll), a swipe left and a pinch (with `inputs.pinch`) carry a 0-1 progress instead of firing the zoom-out at once. The current view shrinks toward its trigger (taking the trigger's border-radius), the previous view loses its effect, the last view takes the previous-view effect. Release past `threshold` or flick → finish; otherwise everything returns. A mouse wheel notch (large or line-based delta) still zooms out at once; momentum after a release is ignored. Implemented with engine-owned Web Animations, then the end state settles with the none driver, so it works with every driver. Skipped under prefers-reduced-motion. Progress is reported by the `zoomOutProgress` event.

#### `rasterize`

Views behind are shown as a SnapDOM photo while they sit there, so a zoom moves pictures instead of DOM. It pays off with heavy views (thousands of nodes, `backdrop-filter`): in Chrome, a frosted-glass board went from about half its frames dropped to none. Light views gain nothing and are left alone. SnapDOM (`@zumer/snapdom`) and its plugins (`@zumer/snapdom-plugins`) are optional peer dependencies, passed in.

- With `stream`: while a view is current, SnapDOM's stream keeps its photo current, repainting only what changed (at most 10 times a second, `fast: false`, outlines left out, animations not followed). When the zoom starts, the last frame is copied into a canvas of its own. If the stream would block more than half the main thread over 2 s, or one full repaint blocks it more than 250 ms, it stops and that view moves as itself for this visit. Blocked time is the plugin's `busyMs` when it reports it, else the frame's `ms`; the plugin's periodic keyframes do not count as slow. Full repaints come from changes in boxes with no solid background, or over other content.
- Without `stream`: one photo per visit, taken at idle once input and the view have been quiet for 300 ms. A view that changed since its photo is never shown as that photo: it moves as itself until a new one is taken. A view that changes during three photos in a row is left live for the visit.
- Never during a transition or a gesture; no photo yet means the real view moves. A view gets a fresh photo on each visit.
- Only views with triggers (`.zoom-me[data-to]`) are photographed or followed: a view without them never moves behind. One that gets a trigger later is followed from then on.
- On zoom-in, the view that moves behind gets class `z-flat`: its children stay laid out but `visibility: hidden`, and a `<canvas class="z-flat-layer">` with the photo covers its border box. The view element still moves, takes the `effects` filter by CSS and answers sibling hit-tests, so geometry and every driver are unchanged. On a zoom-out (and during a followed zoom-out gesture) the view that shrinks away stays live. The views coming back stay photos until the motion ends. Then the real view crossfades in (160 ms) when it has an opaque background; a translucent view swaps at once, since a crossfade would show photo and view together.
- Eligible: `data-rasterize="true"`, or at least `minNodes` elements, or `backdrop-filter` inside. Never: `data-rasterize="false"`, or an iframe inside. A photo that does not fit after a resize is dropped.
- Without SnapDOM, Zumly warns once and views stay live. `destroy()` stops streams and removes photos, observers, listeners and pending captures.

#### `webgl`

Zooms drawn in a WebGL2 canvas inside Zumly's canvas, under the views. While views move, each is a texture and the views themselves are hidden (opacity 0, so they still answer hit-tests). At rest the views behind stay textures, with the engine's effects in a fragment shader instead of a CSS filter; only the current view is DOM. It brings `rasterize` with it and takes the same settings (`snapdom`, `stream`, `minNodes`, `scale`); with `rasterize` given too, those are used (`rasterize: false` does not turn WebGL off: it brings its own). Without WebGL2, views stay DOM. Measured in Chrome on a MacBook: the GPU of a zoom drops from 40-70% (rasterize) to 7-8%; with software rendering (a weak GPU), dropped frames go from 79-82% to 2-13%.

- Textures: a view behind comes from rasterize's stream; the view coming in is a SnapDOM photo taken right before the motion (30-45 ms on a laptop; the trigger looks pressed, a ring shows past 300 ms). Zoom-in, zoom-out, siblings and followed zoom-out gestures all go through WebGL. A transition without animation, `keepAlive: 'visible'` or a texture it could not get runs on the driver, with the views back to DOM.
- `effects`: `transitions.effects` keeps CSS filter syntax; every CSS filter function is built in (blur as a two-pass Gaussian on mip levels). Custom effects: `{ none, uv?, color?, animate? }`. `uv` is GLSL that changes `st` (the point of the view read, 0-1); `color` changes `rgb` and `a`. Both get `v` (the first number) and `vs` (up to four, a `#hex` color counts as three), and can read `photo` (view size, CSS px), `focus` and `focusSize` (the trigger, 0-1), `progress` (zoom progress) and `time`. `animate: true` redraws views behind at rest while the effect shows.
- `glass: false` photographs the view coming in without its `backdrop-filter` (much faster); the real view takes over when the zoom ends.
- `hover: true`: on `pointerover` or `focusin` of a trigger in the current view, the engine resolves the view it opens (view functions run then) and WebGL photographs it out of sight; the click inserts that same node and uses its texture. One at a time; dropped, with its cleanups, when the pointer goes to another trigger or anything moves. Views with `mounted()`, custom elements and deferred views wait for the click.
- `ancestors` (default `true`): the engine keeps three views, and a zoom-in to a fourth level removes the oldest. WebGL draws the views it no longer will into one canvas-sized picture (half the screen's pixels) that moves with the scene, so nothing goes blank; one per level past the third (about 4 MB at dpr 2), and a zoom-out goes back to the one before. `false` lets the oldest view go.
- A lost context sends every view back to DOM; when it comes back, WebGL rebuilds and photographs the views behind again. After a resize, views behind are photographed again where they are.

#### `labels`

Accessible names of the built-in nav controls. Each is a template with `{title}` and `{name}` (of the target view), a function `({ name, title }) => string`, or `false` for none. `labels: false` removes them all.

---

## 5. View Sources

Views can be provided in multiple formats:

### HTML string

```js
views: {
  home: '<div class="z-view"><h1>Hello</h1><div class="zoom-me" data-to="detail">Open</div></div>'
}
```

### URL (fetched)

```js
views: {
  home: 'views/home.html'       // relative URL
  // or: 'https://example.com/views/home.html'
}
```

The HTML file should contain a single root element with class `z-view`:

```html
<div class="z-view">
  <h1>Hello</h1>
  <div class="zoom-me" data-to="detail">Open</div>
</div>
```

### Function

```js
views: {
  detail: (ctx) => {
    // ctx.target — fresh <div> for mounting
    // ctx.trigger — the trigger element (if from click)
    // ctx.context — componentContext from constructor
    // ctx.props — data attributes from trigger (data-id="42" → props.id)
    return `<div class="z-view"><p>Detail for ${ctx.props.id}</p></div>`
  }
}
```

Functions can be async and can return:
- An HTML string
- An HTMLElement
- `void` (if mounting into `ctx.target`)

### Object with render()

```js
views: {
  detail: {
    render(ctx) {
      return `<div class="z-view"><p>Detail</p></div>`
    },
    mounted() {
      // Called after the view is inserted into the DOM
      console.log('View mounted!')
    }
  }
}
```

### View titles

A view can carry a human-readable name for the navigation UI: `title: 'Security'` in an object view (or as a property of a function view), or `data-title="Security"` on the view root, which wins. Without one, the view name is used. Used by the back button, sibling dots, `getViewStack()`, `getViewTitle()` and the view's aria-label.

### HTMLElement

```js
const el = document.createElement('div')
el.classList.add('z-view')
el.innerHTML = '<h1>Hello</h1>'
views: { home: el }  // cloned on each use
```

### Web Component

```js
views: {
  dashboard: 'my-dashboard'  // tag name with hyphen → waits for customElements.whenDefined
}
```

### ViewContext object

All function and object view sources receive a `ViewContext`:

```ts
interface ViewContext {
  target: HTMLDivElement     // Fresh <div> for mounting framework components
  trigger?: HTMLElement      // The trigger element (the one clicked, or the sibling's on a lateral move)
  context: Map | Object      // The componentContext from constructor
  props: Record<string, unknown>  // Trigger data attributes or programmatic props
  onCleanup(callback: () => void | Promise<void>): void  // Teardown when this view is discarded
  onActivate(callback: () => void): void  // Runs each time the view becomes current again without re-rendering (after zoom-out to it, kept-alive sibling returning)
}
```

If a function returns nothing, `target` IS the view: set its classes (`target.className = 'z-view card'`) and render only the content inside it. Do not put another `.z-view` inside `target` (Zumly warns). Views behind the current one are not re-rendered: keep state outside views and repaint in `onActivate`. Object views get `mounted(node)` with the inserted root. HTML templates with several root elements are wrapped in one `.z-view`.

```js
const state = { temperature: 21 }
views.room = ({ target, onActivate }) => {
  target.className = 'z-view room'
  const paint = () => { target.innerHTML = `<h1>${state.temperature}°</h1><b class="zoom-me" data-to="thermostat">Adjust</b>` }
  paint()
  onActivate(paint)
}
```

---

## 6. View Rendering Pipeline

The internal pipeline for rendering a view:

1. **Resolve**: `ViewResolver.resolve(source, context)` → DOM node. Detects source type (html, url, function, object, element, webcomponent) and produces an HTMLElement.
2. **Normalize**: Ensure the node has class `.z-view` (wraps if needed).
3. **Insert**: Sets `dataset.viewName`, adds CSS classes (`is-current-view` or `is-new-current-view has-no-events hide`), appends to canvas.
4. **Mounted**: Calls `views[viewName].mounted()` only AFTER insertion into the DOM.

Function/object contexts always include target, props (empty for initial views), componentContext as context, and onCleanup. Register framework unmount, subscription, or timer cleanup through onCleanup. Cleanup runs once on permanent removal, failed rendering, discarded late results, or destroy; temporary depth detach and lateral keepAlive preserve resources. Async cleanup is started without awaiting it. Function views that mount into target and return nothing preserve that mount container and all roots; set its dimensions explicitly for views smaller than the canvas.

### Deferred Rendering

When `deferred: true` (or per-trigger `data-deferred`), view content is detached before the zoom animation runs, then re-attached after the animation completes. This ensures smooth animations for heavy views.

### Prefetching

Zumly prefetches static HTML and URL views on mouseover/focusin of `.zoom-me` triggers and when scanning active views. Functions, objects, and custom element tags are skipped. You can also eagerly preload static HTML and URL views with the `preload` option:

```js
new Zumly({
  preload: ['detail', 'settings'],  // resolve and cache on init()
  ...
})
```

---

## 7. Lifecycle Events

Subscribe with `instance.on(event, callback)`. Unsubscribe with `instance.off(event, callback)`.

| Event | Data | When |
|-------|------|------|
| `viewChanged` | `{ type, viewName, from, zoomLevel, node }` | After every navigation and after init(); type: 'init' \| 'zoomIn' \| 'zoomOut' \| 'lateral' |
| `viewMounted` | `{ viewName, node }` | After a view is inserted into the DOM |
| `beforeZoomIn` | `{ viewName }` | Before zoom-in animation starts |
| `zoomInStart` | `{ viewName, zoomLevel }` | The new view is in place and starts to move |
| `afterZoomIn` | `{ viewName, zoomLevel }` | After zoom-in animation completes |
| `beforeZoomOut` | `{ zoomLevel, viewName, from, levels? }` | Before zoom-out starts (viewName = view returned to; levels when climbing several) |
| `afterZoomOut` | `{ zoomLevel, viewName, from, levels? }` | After zoom-out completes |
| `beforeLateral` | `{ viewName, from, isBack }` | Before lateral navigation starts |
| `lateralStart` | `{ viewName, from, isBack }` | The sibling is in place and starts to move in |
| `afterLateral` | `{ viewName, from, isBack }` | After lateral navigation completes |
| `zoomOutProgress` | `{ phase, progress, duration?, viewName, from, source }` | Gesture-driven zoom-out (gestures.follow): phase 'start' \| 'move' \| 'commit' \| 'cancel' \| 'end'; source 'wheel' \| 'swipe' \| 'pinch' |
| `destroy` | `{}` | When instance is destroyed |

### Example

```js
const app = new Zumly({ ... })

app.on('afterZoomIn', (data) => {
  console.log(`Zoomed into ${data.viewName} at level ${data.zoomLevel}`)
})

app.on('afterZoomOut', (data) => {
  console.log(`Zoomed out to level ${data.zoomLevel}`)
})

app.on('afterLateral', (data) => {
  console.log(`Navigated from ${data.from} to ${data.viewName}`)
})
```

---

## 8. Public API

### `new Zumly(options: ZumlyOptions)`

Creates a new instance. Does NOT initialize — call `init()` separately.

### `init(): Promise<void>`

Initialize: render the initial view, install plugins, and start prefetching. Must be called after construction, which binds input events. Repeated or concurrent init calls do not duplicate initialization.

### `destroy(): void`

Clean up listeners, observers, timers, navigation UI, view resources registered with onCleanup, and internal state, and remove the views the instance put in the canvas (kept-alive siblings and views still loading included). Idempotent. Releases pending navigation promises and discards late view results. The canvas is left as it was before the instance started: content you put there stays, and a new instance can start on it right away (React StrictMode, hot reload).

### `on(event, fn): this`

Subscribe to a lifecycle event. Chainable.

### `off(event, fn?): this`

Unsubscribe from a lifecycle event. If `fn` is omitted, removes all hooks for that event. Chainable.

### `use(plugin, options?): this`

Register a plugin. If called before init(), plugin installs during init(). If called after, installs immediately. Chainable.

### `zoomLevel(): number`

Returns the current zoom depth (number of stored snapshots). At root = 1, after first zoom-in = 2, etc.

### `getZoomLevel(): number`

Alias for `zoomLevel()`.

### `getCurrentViewName(): string | null`

Returns the name of the currently active view, or null if not initialized.

### `zoomIn(el: HTMLElement): Promise<void>`

Zoom into the view indicated by trigger element (must have `data-to="viewName"`).

### `zoomOut(target?): Promise<void>`

Zoom out one level. No-op at root. `zoomOut(2)` climbs two levels; `zoomOut({ to: 'home' })` climbs to the nearest ancestor with that name; the object form also takes `levels`, `duration` and `ease`. Several levels run as ONE transition (the target's child shrinks into its trigger while deeper views ride along) and clamp at the root. An unknown `to` warns and does nothing. The router uses it for multi-level browser back.

### `getViewStack(): Array<{ name, title, depth, params? }>`

The views from the root (depth 0) to the current one, with their titles. `params` is set for a view opened from a trigger with data (`{ id: 'kitchen' }`).

### `getViewTitle(viewName): string`

The view's `data-title`, else the `title` of its definition, else its name.

### `zoomTo(viewName, options?): Promise<void>`

Programmatic zoom to a named view. Uses a centered synthetic trigger for the transition.

```js
await app.zoomTo('detail', { duration: '500ms', ease: 'ease-out' })
```

Options: `{ duration?: string, ease?: string, props?: Record<string, unknown> }`

### `goTo(viewName, options?): Promise<void>`

Unified navigation API. Supports both depth and lateral navigation.

```js
// Depth (same as zoomTo)
await app.goTo('detail')
await app.goTo('detail', { mode: 'depth' })

// Lateral
await app.goTo('settings', { mode: 'lateral' })
```

Options: `{ mode?: 'depth' | 'lateral', duration?: string, ease?: string, props?: Record<string, unknown> }`

### `back(): Promise<void>`

Navigate back. If there is lateral history at current depth, pops lateral history first (goes back laterally). Otherwise zooms out. Each depth keeps its own lateral history, also after zooming deeper and back out (the same behavior as the router's browser back). The depth back button always zooms out.

### `canGoBack(): boolean`

Whether `back()` would navigate. All navigation promises settle after the transition and completion work. Await each call for sequential navigation. Calls made during a view load or transition are ignored; failures resolve after recovery and are reported by Zumly diagnostics.

---

## 9. Navigation Model

### Depth Navigation (Z axis)

Zooming creates a stack of snapshots. Each snapshot stores:
- Transform states for up to 3 visible views (current, previous, last)
- Scale factor, stagger, effects config

The visible view hierarchy at any point:
```
Canvas
├── .is-last-view       (grandparent — 2 levels up)
├── .is-previous-view   (parent — 1 level up)
└── .is-current-view    (active view)
```

Views beyond 3 levels deep are detached from DOM and restored on zoom-out.

### Lateral Navigation (XY plane)

At any depth, if the parent view has multiple `.zoom-me` triggers, those targets are "siblings". The user can navigate between them:

- Via lateral nav UI (arrows + dots)
- Via clicking sibling triggers visible in the parent view
- Programmatically via `goTo(name, { mode: 'lateral' })`
- Via the Router plugin (browser back)

Lateral history is tracked per depth level and survives zooming deeper and back out. `back()` pops lateral history before zooming out.

A sibling is a view name plus the trigger's data. Triggers to the same view with different `data-*` (other than Zumly's own `data-to`, `data-title`, `data-sibling`, `data-deferred`, `data-hide-trigger` and `data-with-*`) are separate siblings: one dot each, named by the trigger's `data-title`, and the view gets that trigger's data as `props` on every move (click, bar, swipe, `back()`, router):

```html
<div class="zoom-me" data-to="room" data-id="kitchen" data-title="Kitchen">Kitchen</div>
<div class="zoom-me" data-to="room" data-id="bedroom" data-title="Bedroom">Bedroom</div>
```

From code: `goTo('room', { mode: 'lateral', props: { id: 'bedroom' } })`. Plain triggers (only `data-to`) work by name as always, and two triggers to the very same view count as one sibling.

### Input Handling

| Input | Action | Enabled by |
|-------|--------|------------|
| Click `.zoom-me` | Zoom in to `data-to` view | `inputs.click` |
| Click outside current view | Zoom out | `inputs.click` |
| Click sibling trigger in parent | Lateral navigation | `inputs.click` |
| Swipe left | Zoom out (not when it starts on a text field, slider, horizontal scroller or `[data-no-swipe]`); follows the finger with `gestures.follow` | `inputs.touch` |
| Swipe left / right with `lateralNav.swipe` | Next / previous sibling (zooms out on a swipe left when there are no siblings) | `inputs.touch` |
| Pinch (two fingers closing) | Zoom out; follows the fingers with `gestures.follow` | `inputs.pinch` (off by default) |
| Tap `.zoom-me` | Zoom in | `inputs.touch` |
| Tap outside current view | Zoom out | `inputs.touch` |
| ArrowLeft / ArrowDown | Zoom out | `inputs.keyboard` |
| Wheel scroll down | Zoom out; trackpad scrolling follows with `gestures.follow` | `inputs.wheel` |

Wheel events inside scrollable containers are not intercepted.

---

## 10. Transition Drivers

A driver is a function that receives a transition spec and an `onComplete` callback:

```js
function runTransition(spec, onComplete) {
  // Animate views based on spec
  // MUST call onComplete() exactly once when done
}
```

### Built-in Drivers

| Name | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `css` | Pure CSS transitions. Default. Zero JS animation overhead. |
| `waapi` | Web Animations API. JS-controlled timing with CSS-grade performance. |
| `none` | Instant. Applies final state synchronously. Great for testing. |
| `anime` | Anime.js integration. Requires anime.js loaded globally. |
| `gsap` | GSAP integration. Requires gsap loaded globally. |
| `motion` | Motion library integration. Requires motion loaded globally. |

Every driver except `none` slides between siblings with the same motion (the library drivers match `css` and `waapi`: same transforms, duration, easing and fade).

### Custom Driver

```js
new Zumly({
  transitions: {
    driver: (spec, onComplete) => {
      // spec.type: 'zoomIn' | 'zoomOut' | 'lateral'
      // spec.currentView, spec.previousView, spec.lastView
      // spec.currentStage — snapshot with computed transforms
      // spec.duration, spec.ease
      // ... animate, then:
      onComplete()
    }
  }
})
```

### The Spec Object

#### Common fields (all transition types)

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `type` | `'zoomIn' \| 'zoomOut' \| 'lateral'` | Transition type |
| `currentView` | `HTMLElement` | Incoming (zoom-in) or outgoing (zoom-out) view |
| `previousView` | `HTMLElement` | Parent view |
| `lastView` | `HTMLElement \| null` | Grandparent (null at depth <= 2) |
| `currentStage` | `object` | Snapshot with computed states |
| `duration` | `string` | e.g. `'500ms'`, `'1s'` |
| `ease` | `string` | CSS easing |
| `canvas` | `HTMLElement` | Canvas container (zoom-out and lateral) |

#### `currentStage.views[]` — Animation Data

```
views[0] → current view
views[1] → previous view
views[2] → last view (grandparent)
```

Each entry has:

```js
{
  viewName: 'detail',
  backwardState: {
    origin: '125px 100px',
    transform: 'translate(50px, 60px) scale(0.25)',
    duration: '500ms',
    ease: 'ease-in-out',
  },
  forwardState: {
    origin: '125px 100px',
    transform: 'translate(100px, 50px)',
    duration: '500ms',
    ease: 'ease-in-out',
  }
}
```

**Zoom-in**: animate `backwardState.transform` → `forwardState.transform`
**Zoom-out**: animate `forwardState.transform` → `backwardState.transform`

#### Lateral-specific fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `backView` | `HTMLElement \| null` | Parent view behind current depth |
| `backViewState` | `{ transformStart, transformEnd }` | Slide transforms for backView |
| `lastViewState` | `{ transformStart, transformEnd }` | Slide transforms for lastView |
| `incomingTransformStart` | `string` | Incoming view start transform |
| `incomingTransformEnd` | `string` | Incoming view final transform |
| `outgoingTransform` | `string` | Outgoing view current transform |
| `outgoingTransformEnd` | `string` | Outgoing view exit transform |
| `slideDeltaX` | `number` | Horizontal slide distance |
| `slideDeltaY` | `number` | Vertical slide distance |
| `keepAlive` | `boolean` | When true, driver should NOT remove outgoing view from DOM |

### Driver Contract (MUST do)

1. **Call `onComplete()` exactly once** — the engine blocks all events until you do. If you never call it, the UI freezes permanently.
2. **Apply final DOM state** — the engine does NOT do this for you. Use helper functions.
3. **Handle all three types** — `zoomIn`, `zoomOut`, `lateral`.

---

## 11. Driver Helpers

Import from `zumly/driver-helpers`:

```js
import {
  parseDurationMs,
  parseDurationSec,
  applyZoomInEndState,
  applyZoomOutPreviousState,
  applyZoomOutLastState,
  removeViewFromCanvas,
  showViews,
  runLateralInstant,
  createFinishGuard,
  SAFETY_BUFFER_MS,
} from 'zumly/driver-helpers'
```

| Helper | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `parseDurationMs(duration)` | Parse `'1s'`/`'500ms'`/number → milliseconds |
| `parseDurationSec(duration)` | Same but returns seconds |
| `applyZoomInEndState(el, stage)` | Apply final classes + transforms after zoom-in |
| `applyZoomOutPreviousState(el, state)` | Final state for previous view after zoom-out |
| `applyZoomOutLastState(el, state)` | Final state for last view after zoom-out |
| `removeViewFromCanvas(el, canvas)` | Safe removal (handles wrapped elements) |
| `showViews(...elements)` | Remove `hide` class + set `contentVisibility: auto` |
| `runLateralInstant(spec, onComplete)` | Instant lateral transition (no animation) |
| `createFinishGuard(cleanup, timeoutMs)` | Once-only finish + safety timeout |
| `SAFETY_BUFFER_MS` | Default safety buffer (150ms) |

### Matrix interpolation toolkit

| Helper | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `readComputedMatrix(el, origin, transform)` | Read browser-computed matrix |
| `interpolateMatrix(from, to, t)` | Lerp between two matrix objects |
| `matrixToString(m)` | `{ a,b,c,d,e,f }` → `"matrix(...)"` |
| `parseMatrixString(str)` | `"matrix(...)"` → `{ a,b,c,d,e,f }` |
| `identityMatrix()` | Returns identity matrix |
| `lerp(a, b, t)` | Linear interpolation |

### Minimal Custom Driver Example

```js
import {
  parseDurationMs, showViews, applyZoomInEndState,
  applyZoomOutPreviousState, applyZoomOutLastState,
  removeViewFromCanvas, runLateralInstant,
  createFinishGuard, SAFETY_BUFFER_MS,
} from 'zumly/driver-helpers'

export function runTransition(spec, onComplete) {
  const { type, currentView, previousView, lastView, currentStage, duration, canvas } = spec

  if (type === 'lateral') {
    runLateralInstant(spec, onComplete)
    return
  }

  const ms = parseDurationMs(duration)
  showViews(currentView, previousView, lastView)

  if (type === 'zoomIn') {
    currentView.style.opacity = '0'
    currentView.style.transition = `opacity ${ms}ms ease`
    previousView.style.transition = `opacity ${ms}ms ease`

    requestAnimationFrame(() => {
      currentView.style.opacity = '1'
      previousView.style.opacity = '0.3'
    })

    const { finish } = createFinishGuard(() => {
      currentView.style.transition = ''
      previousView.style.transition = ''
      previousView.style.opacity = ''
      applyZoomInEndState(currentView, currentStage)
      applyZoomInEndState(previousView, currentStage)
      if (lastView) applyZoomInEndState(lastView, currentStage)
      onComplete()
    }, ms + SAFETY_BUFFER_MS)

    currentView.addEventListener('transitionend', finish, { once: true })
    return
  }

  if (type === 'zoomOut') {
    currentView.style.transition = `opacity ${ms}ms ease`
    requestAnimationFrame(() => {
      currentView.style.opacity = '0'
      previousView.style.opacity = '1'
    })

    const { finish } = createFinishGuard(() => {
      currentView.style.transition = ''
      removeViewFromCanvas(currentView, canvas)
      applyZoomOutPreviousState(previousView, currentStage.views[1].backwardState)
      if (lastView) applyZoomOutLastState(lastView, currentStage.views[2].backwardState)
      onComplete()
    }, ms + SAFETY_BUFFER_MS)

    currentView.addEventListener('transitionend', finish, { once: true })
    return
  }

  onComplete()
}
```

---

## 12. Plugin System

Plugins extend Zumly with additional behavior. A plugin can be:

### Object plugin

```js
const myPlugin = {
  install(instance, options) {
    instance.on('afterZoomIn', (data) => {
      console.log('Zoomed to', data.viewName)
    })
  }
}

app.use(myPlugin, { /* options */ })
```

### Function plugin

```js
function myPlugin(instance, options) {
  instance.on('afterZoomIn', (data) => {
    console.log('Zoomed to', data.viewName)
  })
}

app.use(myPlugin)
```

Plugins are installed during `init()`, or immediately if `init()` has already been called. Always clean up in the `destroy` event:

```js
const myPlugin = {
  install(instance) {
    function onZoom(data) { /* ... */ }
    instance.on('afterZoomIn', onZoom)
    instance.on('destroy', () => {
      instance.off('afterZoomIn', onZoom)
    })
  }
}
```

---

## 13. Hash Router Plugin

Syncs the browser URL hash with Zumly navigation state. Supports browser back button for zoom-out and lateral back. Forward/deep-linking is intentionally not supported (in a ZUI the zoom origin depends on the trigger element which doesn't exist without context).

### Usage

```js
import Zumly from 'zumly'

const app = new Zumly({ ... })
app.use(Zumly.Router, { separator: '/', prefix: '/' })
app.init()
```

Or with script tag:

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/zumly/dist/zumly.js"></script>
<script>
  const app = new Zumly({ ... })
  app.use(Zumly.Router)
  app.init()
</script>
```

### Options

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `separator` | `'/'` | Character joining view path segments in hash |
| `prefix` | `'/'` | Prefix before path in hash |

### Behavior

- `zoomInStart` / `lateralStart` → `pushState` (new hash entry, as the motion starts, so a browser back during it returns to the view it left); `afterZoomIn` / `afterLateral` → `replaceState` if anything changed
- `afterZoomOut` → `replaceState` (updates hash without new history entry)
- `popstate` event (browser back) → `zoomOut()` or `goTo(name, { mode: 'lateral' })`
- Forward navigation via popstate is blocked (goes back)
- Cleans up all listeners on `destroy`

### URL format

```
#/home              → root view
#/home/dashboard    → zoomed into dashboard from home
#/home/settings     → lateral navigation to settings
#/house/room?id=kitchen → a view opened from a trigger with data-id="kitchen"
```

---

## 14. CSS Classes & Styling

### Required CSS

Always include `zumly.css` (or `zumly.min.css`). This provides the canvas layout, view positioning, and transition classes.

### Canvas

```css
.zumly-canvas {
  /* The container. Must have explicit dimensions. */
  position: relative;
  overflow: hidden;
  width: 100%;
  height: 100vh;
}
```

### View classes

| Class | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `.z-view` | Root class for every view. Required. |
| `.is-current-view` | The active, interactive view |
| `.is-previous-view` | Parent view (one level up) |
| `.is-last-view` | Grandparent view (two levels up) |
| `.is-new-current-view` | Temporarily set during zoom-in transition |
| `.has-no-events` | Disables pointer events during transition |
| `.hide` | Hidden (opacity: 0, content-visibility: hidden) |
| `.is-lateral-hidden` | Kept-alive lateral view (hidden or visible depending on mode) |

### Trigger classes

| Class | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `.zoom-me` | Makes an element a zoom trigger. Must have `data-to="viewName"`. |
| `.zoomed` | Added to trigger after zoom-in (marks which trigger opened current view) |
| `.z-trigger-hidden` | Trigger hidden via `hideTrigger: true` |
| `.z-trigger-fade` | Trigger fading out via `hideTrigger: 'fade'` |

### Navigation UI classes

| Class | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `.z-depth-nav` | Depth navigation container (back button) |
| `.z-depth-nav--bottom-left` | Position modifier |
| `.z-depth-nav--top-left` | Position modifier |
| `.z-nav-back` | Back button element |
| `.z-lateral-nav` | Lateral navigation container |
| `.z-lateral-nav--bottom-center` | Position modifier |
| `.z-lateral-nav--top-center` | Position modifier |
| `.z-nav-arrow` | Arrow button |
| `.z-nav-prev` / `.z-nav-next` | Previous/next arrows |
| `.z-nav-lateral-dots` | Dots container |
| `.z-nav-dot` | Individual dot |
| `.z-nav-lat-dot` | Lateral dot |
| `.is-active` | Active dot indicator |

### Effect classes

| Class | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `.has-effect` | View has a CSS filter effect applied |
| `.has-effect-reverse` | Animating effect removal |
| `.z-view-fade-in` | View fading in (hideTrigger: 'fade') |
| `.z-view-fade-out` | View fading out on zoom-out |
| `.z-flat` | View behind shown as a photo (`rasterize`): children hidden, layout kept |
| `.z-flat-layer` | The `<canvas>` with the photo, inside a `.z-flat` view |

### CSS Custom Properties

| Property | Set on | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `--z-effect-filter` | View with effect | CSS filter value |
| `--zoom-duration` | Various | Transition duration |
| `--zoom-ease` | Various | Transition easing |
| `--z-nav-bg` | Canvas, `.z-depth-nav` or `.z-lateral-nav` | Background of the back button, its bands and the sibling bar |
| `--z-nav-color` | Canvas, `.z-depth-nav` or `.z-lateral-nav` | Color of glyphs, rings, arrows and dots |
| `--z-nav-active` | Canvas or `.z-lateral-nav` | Current sibling dot color (default: `--z-nav-color`) |
| `--z-nav-border` | Canvas, `.z-depth-nav` or `.z-lateral-nav` | Hairline border color |
| `--z-nav-shadow` | Canvas, `.z-depth-nav` or `.z-lateral-nav` | Drop shadow |
| `--z-nav-blur` | Canvas, `.z-depth-nav` or `.z-lateral-nav` | `backdrop-filter` |
| `--z-nav-hover` | Canvas, `.z-depth-nav` or `.z-lateral-nav` | Hover overlay |

---

## 15. Per-Trigger Overrides

Trigger elements (`.zoom-me`) support data attributes that override global transition options:

| Attribute | Overrides | Example |
|-----------|-----------|---------|
| `data-to` | — (required) | `data-to="detail"` |
| `data-with-duration` | `transitions.duration` | `data-with-duration="500ms"` |
| `data-with-ease` | `transitions.ease` | `data-with-ease="ease-out"` |
| `data-with-cover` | `transitions.cover` | `data-with-cover="height"` |
| `data-with-stagger` | `transitions.stagger` | `data-with-stagger="100"` |
| `data-with-effects` | `transitions.effects` | `data-with-effects="blur(3px) \| blur(8px)"` |
| `data-hide-trigger` | `transitions.hideTrigger` | `data-hide-trigger="fade"` |
| `data-deferred` | `deferred` | `data-deferred` |

Any data attribute on a trigger is also passed as `ctx.props` to the view function.

---

## 16. Accessibility

Zumly includes built-in accessibility support:

- Canvas gets `role="application"`, `aria-roledescription="zoomable interface"`, `aria-live="polite"`, `tabindex="0"`
- Each view gets `aria-label="View: {viewName}"` (unless already set)
- Navigation buttons have `aria-label` attributes
- Focus is managed after transitions: moves to first focusable element in current view, or the view itself
- Keyboard navigation: Enter/Space activate triggers; ArrowLeft/ArrowDown zoom out outside text fields and editable controls
- Generic triggers receive tabindex; native controls retain their semantics and navigation buttons use click activation
- Background views are inert and aria-hidden until active again
- Reduced-motion preference selects instant transitions automatically

---

## 17. Framework Integration Patterns

### React

```jsx
import Zumly from 'zumly'
import 'zumly/style.css'
import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react'
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client'

function DetailView({ id }) {
  return <div className="z-view"><h1>Detail {id}</h1></div>
}

function App() {
  const ref = useRef(null)

  useEffect(() => {
    const app = new Zumly({
      mount: '#zumly-app',
      initialView: 'home',
      views: {
        home: '<div class="z-view"><button class="zoom-me" data-to="detail" data-id="42">Open</button></div>',
        detail: (ctx) => {
          const root = createRoot(ctx.target)
          ctx.onCleanup(() => root.unmount())
          root.render(<DetailView id={ctx.props.id} />)
          // Return void — Zumly uses ctx.target
        }
      }
    })
    app.init()
    ref.current = app
    return () => app.destroy()
  }, [])

  return <div className="zumly-canvas" id="zumly-app" style={{ width: '100%', height: '100vh' }} />
}
```

### Vue

```js
import Zumly from 'zumly'
import 'zumly/style.css'
import { createApp } from 'vue'
import DetailComponent from './Detail.vue'

const app = new Zumly({
  mount: '#app',
  initialView: 'home',
  views: {
    home: '<div class="z-view"><div class="zoom-me" data-to="detail">Open</div></div>',
    detail: (ctx) => {
      const component = createApp(DetailComponent, { id: ctx.props.id })
      ctx.onCleanup(() => component.unmount())
      component.mount(ctx.target)
    }
  }
})
app.init()
```

### Svelte

```js
import Zumly from 'zumly'
import 'zumly/style.css'
import Detail from './Detail.svelte'

const app = new Zumly({
  mount: '#app',
  initialView: 'home',
  views: {
    home: '<div class="z-view"><div class="zoom-me" data-to="detail">Open</div></div>',
    detail: (ctx) => {
      const component = new Detail({ target: ctx.target, props: { id: ctx.props.id } })
      ctx.onCleanup(() => component.$destroy())
    }
  }
})
app.init()
```

### Web Components

```js
// Define your component
class MyDashboard extends HTMLElement {
  connectedCallback() {
    this.classList.add('z-view')
    this.innerHTML = '<h1>Dashboard</h1>'
  }
}
customElements.define('my-dashboard', MyDashboard)

// Use tag name as view source
const app = new Zumly({
  mount: '#app',
  initialView: 'home',
  views: {
    home: '<div class="z-view"><div class="zoom-me" data-to="dashboard">Open</div></div>',
    dashboard: 'my-dashboard'  // Zumly waits for customElements.whenDefined
  }
})
```

### SPA Lifecycle

In a SPA, always destroy the instance when the component unmounts:

```js
// Create
const app = new Zumly({ ... })
await app.init()

// Later, when unmounting:
app.destroy()   // also removes its views: the canvas is ready for a new instance
```

---

## Diagnostics

Zumly reports mistakes in the console (warnings and errors are always shown; `debug: true` adds navigation traces):

- `initialView` not in `views` → error with "Did you mean …?"; the instance does not start.
- Unknown option keys (`lateralnav`, `transitions.drivr`) → warning with the closest key.
- Invalid `duration` or CSS `ease` → warning and fallback.
- A `.zoom-me` whose `data-to` names no view → one warning when its view becomes current, with a suggestion. A hyphenated name not in `views` is treated as a custom element tag; if it is never defined, navigation fails after 10 s instead of hanging.
- Canvas without size (still 0 after 1 s) → warning explaining `position: relative` + height.
- Mount element without `zumly-canvas` → class added, warning.

## 18. Ecosystem

### Orbit CSS

Docs: https://zumerlab.com/orbit/ · Repository: https://github.com/zumerlab/orbit

Radial layout system (`@zumer/orbit`): `.bigbang > .gravity-spot > .orbit-N > .satellite > .capsule`, plus `<o-arc>` and `<o-progress>`. Works inside Zumly views without glue: Orbit redraws on insert/resize, through zoom, lateral and keepAlive.

- Make satellites' capsules the triggers (`<div class="capsule zoom-me" data-to="kitchen">`): the next view grows exactly out of the satellite.
- `<o-arc>` as trigger zooms from the whole ring box (its box is the ring); put a satellite on the segment instead.
- Size dial views (`.dial { width: min(78vmin, 620px); aspect-ratio: 1 }`); in Orbit 2 the `.bigbang` takes the view's width. Orbit 1.x: set `--o-force` on `.gravity-spot`.
- Repaint gauges in `onActivate`, or update `<o-progress value>` attributes (Orbit redraws).
- `hideTrigger: 'fade'` crossfades the satellite into the new dial; give dial views a background.
- Add `data-no-swipe` to knobs/rings the user drags.
- Guide: https://zumerlab.com/zumly/integrations/orbit-css.html · live example: https://zumerlab.com/zumly/integrations/examples/orbit.html

### SnapDOM

[https://github.com/zumerlab/snapdom](https://github.com/zumerlab/snapdom)

DOM-to-image capture library (`@zumer/snapdom`).

---

## 19. TypeScript Support

Zumly ships TypeScript definitions at `types/zumly.d.ts`.

### Key types

```ts
import type {
  Zumly,
  ZumlyOptions,
  ViewSource,
  ViewFunction,
  ViewObject,
  ViewContext,
  TransitionOptions,
  TransitionSpec,
  DriverName,
  DriverFunction,
  DepthNavOptions,
  LateralNavOptions,
  InputsOptions,
  GoToOptions,
  ZoomToOptions,
  ZumlyEventMap,
  ZumlyEventName,
  ZumlyPlugin,
  RouterOptions,
  ZoomSnapshot,
  ViewState,
  ViewEntry,
} from 'zumly'
```

### DriverName

```ts
type DriverName = 'css' | 'waapi' | 'none' | 'anime' | 'gsap' | 'motion'
```

### DriverFunction

```ts
type DriverFunction = (spec: TransitionSpec, onComplete: () => void) => void
```

### ViewSource

```ts
type ViewSource = string | ViewFunction | ViewObject | HTMLElement
```

### ZumlyOptions

```ts
interface ZumlyOptions {
  mount: string
  initialView: string
  views: Record<string, ViewSource>
  preload?: string[]
  transitions?: TransitionOptions
  debug?: boolean
  componentContext?: Map<string, unknown> | Record<string, unknown>
  lateralNav?: boolean | LateralNavOptions
  depthNav?: boolean | DepthNavOptions
  inputs?: InputsOptions
  deferred?: boolean
}
// Note: hideTrigger lives inside TransitionOptions (transitions.hideTrigger)
```

---

## Appendix: Complete Constructor Example

```js
const app = new Zumly({
  mount: '#app',
  initialView: 'home',
  views: {
    home: 'views/home.html',
    dashboard: (ctx) => `<div class="z-view"><h1>Dashboard for ${ctx.props.id}</h1></div>`,
    settings: {
      render: (ctx) => '<div class="z-view"><h1>Settings</h1></div>',
      mounted: () => console.log('Settings view mounted')
    },
    detail: '<div class="z-view"><p>Inline HTML detail</p></div>',
  },
  preload: ['dashboard'],
  debug: false,
  deferred: false,
  componentContext: { api: myApiClient },
  transitions: {
    driver: 'waapi',
    cover: 'width',
    duration: '800ms',
    ease: 'cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)',
    effects: ['blur(2px)', 'blur(6px) saturate(0.5)'],
    stagger: 50,
    hideTrigger: 'fade',
  },
  depthNav: { position: 'bottom-left' },
  lateralNav: {
    mode: 'always',
    arrows: true,
    dots: true,
    keepAlive: false,
    position: 'bottom-center',
  },
  inputs: {
    wheel: true,
    keyboard: true,
    click: true,
    touch: true,
  },
})

app.use(Zumly.Router, { separator: '/', prefix: '/' })

app.on('afterZoomIn', ({ viewName, zoomLevel }) => {
  console.log(`Entered ${viewName} at depth ${zoomLevel}`)
})

await app.init()
```
